entities.summary: Theon of Alexandria was a Greek scholar and mathematician who lived in Alexandria, Egypt during the Classical era. He edited and arranged Euclid's Elements and wrote commentaries on works by Euclid and Ptolemy. His daughter Hypatia also won fame as a mathematician. Theon's work on Euclid's Elements, known as the 'Commentary on the First Book of Euclid,' is still studied today for its clarity and insight into Euclid's thought process. Theon's contributions to mathematics and education helped shape the intellectual landscape of the ancient world. He was a prominent figure in the city of Alexandria, where he was known for his wisdom and knowledge. Theon's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of mathematics and science in the centuries that followed. His daughter Hypatia's tragic death in 415 CE marked a turning point in the suppression of pagan knowledge in the Roman Empire. Theon's work on the elements of geometry and his commentaries on Euclid and Ptolemy remain important references in the study of ancient Greek mathematics and astronomy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Theon of Alexandria's work on Euclid's Elements and his commentaries on Euclid and Ptolemy helped shape the intellectual landscape of the ancient world. His daughter Hypatia's tragic death in 415 CE marked a turning point in the suppression of pagan knowledge in the Roman Empire. Theon's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of mathematics and science in the centuries that followed.
